O.outcome_detail: attitudes and perceptions toward teaching and learning

cells.quote: Consistent with previous literature reviews, studies regularly demonstrated a positive impact on perceptions and attitudes towards teaching (Kirkpatrick level 2a).
cells.note: The review included controlled and uncontrolled studies, so the comparison varied and was often absent.

O.outcome_detail: modification of teaching knowledge or skills

cells.quote: Positive impact was also demonstrated supporting modification of knowledge or skills (Kirkpatrick level 2b)
cells.note: The text reports positive pooled findings but substantial methodological heterogeneity and bias.

O.outcome_detail: transfer of teaching skills and behaviours to the workplace

cells.quote: Although substantial bias is present in most studies, which prevents definite conclusions regarding the real impact of teaching programs on developing JMOs teaching skills (Kirkpatrick level 3), the results are more likely to be positive than negative.
cells.note: Positive direction is qualified by substantial bias and limited objective evidence.

cells.quote: Studies did demonstrate that positive organisational change could occur due to the intervention (Kirkpatrick level 4a).
cells.note: The review describes organisational outcomes from individual studies rather than a common effect estimate.

O.outcome_detail: change in attitudes toward teaching and learning

cells.quote: Studies published prior to 2008 of which were included in the five literature reviews demonstrated many threats to validity. That said the quality of these was generally more robust than that of the studies published after 2008.
cells.note: The synthesis included 39 heterogeneous studies, including randomized, non-randomized, and uncontrolled trials; 18 reported level 2a outcomes, while five studies overall reported findings that were not positive.

O.outcome_detail: modification of teaching knowledge or skills

cells.quote: The individual analysis of all 39 studies demonstrates clearly that there is convincing evidence that supports the efficacy of JMO teaching skills courses in improving Kirkpatrick outcomes up to level 3.
cells.note: Level 2b combined knowledge and skills outcomes; the review did not provide a pooled effect size or outcome-specific comparative estimate.

O.outcome_detail: transfer of teaching skills to workplace behavior

cells.quote: Although substantial bias is present in most studies, which prevents definite conclusions regarding the real impact of teaching programs on developing JMOs teaching skills (Kirkpatrick level 3), the results are more likely to be positive than negative.
cells.note: Twenty-one of the 39 pre-2008 studies reported level 3 outcomes; the synthesis included uncontrolled studies and did not establish a pooled effect size.

cells.quote: Studies did demonstrate that positive organisational change could occur due to the intervention (Kirkpatrick level 4a).
cells.note: Two pre-2008 studies reported level 4a outcomes, both shown as positive in the study's table; the review provided no pooled effect size.

O.outcome_detail: change in organisational practice with dual benefits for resident and students

cells.quote: One study created a teaching resident position that enabled the dual benefit to the resident and the students that the resident was teaching.
cells.note: The study text reports a positive organisational change but does not state a comparison condition or provide an effect size.

O.outcome_detail: dissemination of teaching-skills courses across the organisation

cells.quote: Another created a “train the trainer” program which enabled the dissemination of teaching skills courses across the organisation.
cells.note: The study text reports a positive organisational change but does not state a comparison condition or provide an effect size.

O.outcome_detail: invitations to deliver the program elsewhere, recruitment value, and education-board interest

cells.quote: Ostapchuck et al. found that their teaching skills program led to invitations for the delivery of the program to other areas of the organisation, became a point of difference to attract residents to their program and gained interest from the education board.
cells.note: The study text reports multiple positive organisational outcomes but does not state a comparison condition or provide an effect size.
